newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX gasoline ends higher on spread buying.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX gasoline ends higher on spread buying.

text.p: NYMEX gasoline rose Tuesday, bucking declines in the rest of the oil complex, as cash market strength prompted dealers to unwind positions in heating oil and buy gasoline.

"I think a lot of it was spread buying, selling heating oil and buying gasoline," said James Cordier, trader with Allendale Inc in St. Petersberg, Fla., adding "I really feel things with heating oil are over for now, and the next bull is gasoline."
February gasoline settled up 0.21 cent at 67.44 cents a gallon.

"There was very good crack buying since the (U.S.) Gulf has been screaming higher in the past couple of days," said a New York gasoline dealer. The Feb gasoline-to-crude crack spread rose sharply to $3.52 a barrel from $3.00 Monday.

February crude ended off 43 cents at $24.80 a barrel ahead of the contract's expiry Tuesday as dealers rolled their positions out of February into March. February heating oil finished off 0.91 cent a gallon at 66.03 cents.
Heating oil has lost more than 3.50 cents a gallon since last week on ample supply and milder weather in the "heating oil belt" of the northeastern United States.

Meteorologists have called for above average temperatures this week in the U.S. Northeast, the largest heating oil market in the world, when heating oil in the U.S. Gulf and New York Harbor has been more than sufficient, dealers said.

Conventional unleaded gasoline in the U.S. Gulf, on the other hand, was up one cent a gallon from Monday. A slew of refinery turnarounds in that region has sent refiners buying supply to cover the maintenance-related production loss, dealers said.
Production from these refineries is expected to resume with a bias towards gasoline as refiners stock up ahead of the spring and summer season when demand for gasoline traditionally peaks.
For the week ended January 10, the American Petroleum Institute (API) showed gasoline stocks relatively tight, off 9.35 million barrels off from a year ago.
In contrast, the data showed that distillate stocks, comprised of heating oil and diesel, were now only 350,000 barrels below year ago levels after being 20 million barrels below year ago in August.

Due to the Martin Luther King holiday Monday, the API is expected to report its weekly oil inventory data for the week ended January 17 after the market's close Wednesday instead of Tuesday when it traditionally releases the report.
((-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761))
